finding: Line 29 `name not in local` compares the extension-bearing Path(suite).name (e.g. 'verify_foo.py') against `local`, whose entries are extension-less suite names, so the comparison is always true and the 'not silently also in the mirror' guard never fires.

instructionSha256/approvedChangeSha256 are recomputed from route_instruction/route_change and compared only against hash fields stored in that same document, with no externally pinned literal, so a self-authenticating edit of text plus its stored hash passes.

The added check's boolean predicate `entry_outside_cf <= on_disk` never references the freshly computed `historical_core_full` (used only in the diagnostic message), so it cannot detect the CORE/FULL name substitution the check claims to guard against.

Line 11 `return` after the try/except executes whenever validate_contract_value did NOT raise ContractError, so a mutation the validator fails to reject is silently treated as a passing guard instead of raising.

The reproduce-command check only requires `bool(reproduce)` non-empty, with no placeholder/executability check, so an unfilled template like '--phase <phase>' satisfies it without ever being a runnable command.

Only full-comment lines (`stripped.startswith('#')`) are skipped before the whole-line regex scan, so a trailing inline comment naming a suite (e.g. `cmd arg  # tests/verify_new.py`) is still counted as executed, and `unparsed` is unconditionally returned as `[]`.
